# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for question answering)

## BOOK 1: "The Mystery at Lovers' Cave" by Anthony Berkeley (Gutenberg 70877)

**Chapters:** I Our Special Correspondent; II Girls and Murder; III Inspector Moresby Is Reluctant; IV Anthony Interviews a Suspect; V Roger Takes Up the Cudgels; VI An Unwelcome Clue; VII Sidelights on a Loathsome Lady; VIII Introducing a Goat-faced Clergyman; IX Colin, Who Art Thou?; X Tea, China and Young Love; XI Inspector Moresby Conducts an Interview; XII Real Bad Blood; XIII A Midnight Expedition; XIV Roger Is Argumentative; XV Interesting Discovery of a Shoe; XVI Inspector Moresby Intervenes; XVII Shocking Ignorance of a Clergyman; XVIII Preparations for an Arrest; XIX End of a Scoundrel; XX Poisons and Pipes; XXI Roger Plays a Lone Hand; XXII New Discoveries; XXIII Colin Upsets the Apple-cart; XXIV Inspector Moresby Is Humorous; XXV Roger Solves the Mystery; XXVI Caustic Soda.

**Characters:**
- Roger Sheringham: novelist/amateur sleuth, ~36, stocky, pipe, Courier special correspondent. Cousin of Anthony.
- Anthony Walton: Roger's cousin, ~25, big, slow-witted, Oxford rugby blue, golf half-blue, plays for Harlequins; falls for Margaret Cross.
- Inspector Moresby: Scotland Yard, genial, walrus moustache, on holiday at Sandsea with wife and two children.
- Mrs. Elsie Vane (née Cross/"Elsie"): victim, 28, fell from cliff at Ludmouth Bay; married Dr. George Vane for money; real name line from Liverpool bucket-shop family; was a bigamous/invalid marriage (earlier form with Herbert Peters).
- Margaret Cross: 21–22, Elsie's cousin, dark hair, brown eyes, proud; ex-governess/waitress/parlour-maid; inherited under Elsie's will (~£10,000, later invalidated).
- Dr. George Vane: big, black beard, laboratory, china collector.
- Miss Mary Williamson: secretary, pince-nez, short fair hair, science graduate, in love with Vane.
- Mrs. Russell (jealous, large feet, pince-nez) and Mr. Russell (red-faced, Rose Cottage).
- Colin Woodthorpe: son of Sir Henry Woodthorpe, Clouston Hall; Elsie's lover; wrote note signed "Colin" ("Elsie darling... P.S. Destroy this.").
- Rev. Samuel Meadows: goat-faced, beaming, false clergyman; real name Herbert Peters, alias Slippery Sam, The Shrimp, Sky Pilot, Herbert Smith; criminal (ex-convict, Elsie's first "husband"); murdered by aconitine in his pipe stem.
- Mrs. Harper: landlady at Meadows' lodgings; Mrs. Mullins mentioned.
- Dr. Young: doctor who examined Meadows' body.
- Landlord of the Crown inn (ox-like); porter/station-master (combination).
- William? (no—that's Book 2).

**Key events:**
- Roger gets Courier assignment by phone from editor Burgoyne; Anthony agrees to come; they take Ludmouth rooms at the Crown (booked 5 rooms, ~£10 deposit).
- Woman found dead at foot of cliffs; body found by fisherman; verdict accidental initially.
- Moresby at ledge; footprints of two women in mud (larger shoe of second woman); a large coat button (light-blue bone, white pattern) clenched in Elsie's hand, identified as from Margaret's sports-coat.
- Roger finds a piece of notepaper on rocks (Colin's letter, "Monday"; "Elsie darling... Meet me at the usual place to-morrow, same time... Colin").
- Anthony meets Margaret on cliffs; she is weeping on his shoulder.
- Roger pretends fall to hide notepaper; Moresby shows inspector's cards.
- Mrs. Russell's shoes (large feet) used by murderer; Roger sends Anthony's maid shoes to match prints.
- Roger finds Meadows (Samuel) is criminal via thumbprint on a newspaper; Meadows dies (aconitine in pipe) before arrest.
- Colin Woodthorpe falsely confesses; Margaret leaves with him (engaged secretly to Colin; she was the true murderer per Moresby).
- Moresby's solution: Margaret killed Elsie and Meadows; Margaret's murder motive: Colin, inheritance. Moresby says the marriage settlement invalid (Elsie never legal wife).
- Roger's theories (Mrs. Russell, Vane, Herbert Peters) are proven wrong; Moresby's shoe/aconitine reasoning reveals Margaret.

**Ending:** Moresby says: "Do you know what's the matter with you, sir? You've been reading too many of those detective stories." THE END.

---

## BOOK 2: "The Layton Court Mystery" by Anthony Berkeley (Gutenberg 72883)

**Chapters:** I Eight o'Clock in the Morning; II An Interrupted Breakfast; III Mr. Sheringham is Puzzled; IV Major Jefferson is Reluctant; V Mr. Sheringham Asks a Question; VI Four People Behave Remarkably; VII The Vase That Wasn't; VIII Mr. Sheringham Becomes Startling; IX Mr. Sheringham Sees Visions; X Mrs. Plant is Apprehensive; XI Lady Stanworth Exchanges Glances; XII Hidden Chambers And What-Nots; XIII Mr. Sheringham Investigates a Footprint; XIV Dirty Work at the Ash Pit; XV Mr. Sheringham Amuses an Ancient Rustic; XVI Mr. Sheringham Lectures on Neo-Platonism; XVII Mr. Grierson Becomes Heated; XVIII What the Settee Had to Tell; XIX Mr. Sheringham Loses and Wins the Same Bet; XX Mrs. Plant Proves Disappointing; XXI Mr. Sheringham is Dramatic; XXII Mr. Sheringham Solves the Mystery; XXIII Mrs. Plant Talks; XXIV Mr. Sheringham is Disconcerted; XXV The Mystery Finally Refuses to Accept Mr. Sheringham's Solution; XXVI Mr. Grierson Tries His Hand; XXVII Mr. Sheringham Hits the Mark; XXVIII What Really Did Happen. (Dedication: "To my Father.")

**Characters:**
- Roger Sheringham (narrator focus), ~36, stocky, Winchester/Oxford, pipe.
- Alexander "Alec" Grierson: Anthony-like cousin-type friend (Roger's friend), big, cricketer (Oxford), Scottish-ish; engaged to Barbara Shannon.
- Barbara Shannon: ~19, small, fair, grey eyes; engaged to Alec, then breaks off; secretly tied to Stanworth's blackmail.
- Mrs. Shannon: Barbara's mother, plump, peevish.
- Victor Stanworth: host, ~60, genial, owner of Layton Court; found shot in library (revolver to forehead) chair behind writing table; "suicide" confession typed.
- Lady Stanworth (Cynthia, née Anglemere, Earl of Grassingham's daughter): sister-in-law; hostess; later marries Jefferson secretly.
- Major Harry Jefferson: secretary, tall, sallow, taciturn; ex-army; forged check incident in India; secretly married to Lady Stanworth.
- Graves (Bill Higgins): butler, ex-boxer, blackmail victim of Stanworth.
- Mrs. Mary Plant: ~26, dark-haired, husband in Soudan Civil Service; blackmailed by Stanworth; jewels in safe.
- William: gardener (melancholy, greenfly); Mrs. William at lodge.
- Inspector Mansfield (Elchester police); Dr. Matthewson (doctor); Rudgeman (constable); Halbert (showman? chauffeur: Chapman).
- John Prince: farm worker at Hillcrest Farm (Mr. Wetherby); red herring; attacked Stanworth once; bull incident with Roger & Alec.

**Key events:**
- Morning: William gardening; Roger and Alec in garden; Alec posts letter to bookmaker; Barbara breaks engagement.
- Breakfast interrupted; Lady Stanworth calls Roger and Alec; library door broken in; Stanworth found shot in chair. Confession typed ("For reasons that concern only myself, I have decided to kill myself"), signature "Victor Stanworth" with spoiled "V-i-c" above.
- Inspector Mansfield arrives; safe opened (contains share certificates, cash ~£4,000+, Mrs. Plant's jewel case).
- Roger finds: shot in centre of forehead (odd position); vase on chimney-piece smashed by bullet; second shot fired; only one shell in revolver; ink-stained blotter; fountain pen scratch marks; second sheet with signature in waste-paper basket; scratch on Stanworth's wrist.
- Footprints under library window (sash/lattice window), handle trick to lock window from outside; footprints smoothed later.
- Ash pit: letter in pencil ("…that brute Prince… this neighbourhood… serious danger…"); Prince's Hillcrest visit; bull chase.
- Settee: woman's handkerchief (jasmine scent "Parfum Jasmine"), face powder, hair.
- Roger's false theory: Jefferson/Mrs. Plant/Lady Stanworth conspiracy; Mrs. Plant confessed she was blackmailed by Stanworth (~£250, bribed/jewels); she was not the killer.
- Jefferson confesses secret marriage to Lady Stanworth; Stanworth blackmailed him over forged check.
- Truth revealed in final chapter: Alec Grierson killed Stanworth in self-defence after witnessing blackmail of Barbara Shannon (her mother's secret). Alec staged suicide; Roger concludes; Alec asks whether to confess; Roger says no.

**Ending:** Roger says, "For heaven's sake, do try sometimes not to be so disgustingly conventional!" THE END.
